title: Election Commission Seeks to Remove Half the Bengal Voters Judges Have Cleared For Inclusion
shows: From appeal records collected by the Civic Research Group, counts the Election Commission's appeals before West Bengal's SIR tribunals against voters whom judicial officers had found eligible, 14,75,887 of 30,00,545 by 17 October, set out by district and seat, by the minority share of each seat and by the 2026 result, with how few appeals the tribunals had decided.
quote: The Commission is the appellant in these cases.
The Commission has not said on what grounds it is challenging these voters, who decided to file the appeals, or whether each case was individually reviewed before an appeal was filed.
note: Read in full on 22 October 2026. Went live 21 October 2026, 7:23 pm. Part of a series on adjudication in West Bengal. Also entered as court-47 in disputes_research/courts.json.

title: SIR Enumeration Form may have violated electoral rules prescribing Form-4 for collecting voter details
shows: Sets the enumeration form used in the revision beside Rule 8 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, which prescribes Form 4 for collecting electors' details from households, and Rule 25, which says an intensively revised roll is prepared afresh. The form came pre-printed from the 2025 roll and asks for links to the 2002 roll, which Form 4 does not. Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer replied that Form 4 had not been used for a long time and that the format followed the Commission's decision.
quote: Rule 8 of the RER, 1960, prescribes Form-4 issued by the Electoral Registration Officers to collect details of the electors in all kinds of revisions of the electoral rolls, be it Special Summary Revision or Special Intensive Revision.
note: Read in full on 22 October 2026 via Firecrawl. Published 22 October 2026, 8:59 am IST, updated 11:22 am. Hyderabad dateline.
